summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted due to weakness and tachycardia. He had a history of AV graft steal syndrome, diabetes, and atrial fibrillation. On admission, he was somnolent and found to have severe hypoglycemia, which likely triggered an episode of atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. His insulin regimen was adjusted from 28 units of glargine in the morning to 10 units at bedtime to prevent recurrent lows. He was volume overloaded, with pulmonary edema seen on chest X-ray, and underwent hemodialysis with improvement. Steal syndrome symptoms were managed with continued use of midodrine and digoxin before dialysis. His mental status and strength improved with treatment. He was discharged to an extended care facility with medication changes, including reduced gabapentin dosing, and plans for close monitoring of blood glucose and heart rate.
